protocol.title: Node lesson 3 — Sets, lists & plates
protocol.summary: A guided build: construct two option sets, combine them into an experiment list, and light up the plate planner — with totals that scale with replicates and prep excess.

sections.label: From sets to a plate plan

chips.text: you build it — nothing is pre-made

children.body: How this lesson works. The guided tour is running in the ⬡ Nodes view. Most bench work is “every combination of a few choices” — you'll build two generator nodes (a Choices set and an Ordered set), feed them into a List, and the plate planner below lights up with your experiments.

The build: treatment is a Choices set (Control, Drug) and dose is an Ordered set (low → mid → high). Both wire into a List named conditions with a structural feed. Two treatments × three doses = six experiments. The tour asks for these exact names because the plate planner below is wired to them.

You'll also add two Inputs the planner reads: reps (wells per experiment) and excess (prep factor, e.g. 1.2 for +20%). These aren't wired into the graph — the planner looks them up by name, which is why the tour has you name them precisely.

A structural feed is made like any wire: drag a generator's right dot onto the List's open “feed…” dot. After the build, add a third option to treatment and the list jumps to nine rows — the plate plan rebuilds instantly.

Scroll to the Plate planner below (it fills once your conditions list exists). Pick experiments, add plates from the ＋ Add plate menu (96 / 384 / 24-well presets), then drag experiment chips onto wells — or press Arrange to lay them out by fill direction, factor→axis, spread, or randomized, then hand-tweak by dragging. Drag a well off the plate to remove it.

The totals table multiplies each experiment's per-well quantity by how many wells you assigned (reps) and by the prep excess factor, then pools by treatment. Change reps or excess in the Nodes view and the master-batch totals move — this is where “prep 20% extra” actually does something.

You've now built the core of a real protocol: sets → list → plate layout → prep totals. Lesson 4 adds the Code node, for the one calculation that's easier to write as a line of JavaScript than a formula.
